spec.title: Cold resume — `CONTINUE.md` and the session commands

p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The second file of the discipline: `CONTINUE.md`, the cold-resume snapshot at the repository root. What goes in it, when it is written, the wind-down and resume commands that bracket a session, and the precedence rule when the snapshot and the WAL disagree.

p.WAL-IS-WRITTEN-FOR-THE-SAME-PROJECT-RHYT: The WAL is written for the next session on the *same* project rhythm: terse, current, one page, assuming the reader knows the terrain.

p.A-COLD-READER-DOES-NOT-KNOW-THE-TERRAIN: A cold reader does not know the terrain: you on a different machine, a teammate cloning the repository, a session resuming after weeks or after a context compaction.

p.THE-COLD-READER-NEEDS-THE-TOUR: The cold reader needs the tour — where things are, what commands run, what was decided and why — before the one-page checkpoint means anything.

p.THE-PAIR-PASSES-THE-ACCEPTANCE-TEST: The pair together passes the discipline's acceptance test: **a stranger with only the repository resumes work without asking.**

p.CONTINUE-LIVES-AT-THE-REPOSITORY-ROOT: `CONTINUE.md` lives at the repository root, where a cold reader looks first.

p.CONTINUE-IS-OVERWRITTEN-WHOLESALE: It is **overwritten wholesale** every time it is written — never appended to, never patched; staleness compounds otherwise.

facts.BODY-TLDR-SUMMARY: A short TL;DR / executive summary at the top.
facts.BODY-WHERE-WORK-STANDS: Where work stands: branch, ahead/behind the remote, working-tree status.
facts.BODY-ACTIVE-BLOCKER: The active blocker, if any, and the exact human action that unblocks it.
facts.BODY-NEXT-STEPS-RECIPE: The exact next-steps recipe — commands, file paths, line numbers — for whoever picks up cold.
facts.BODY-NON-OBVIOUS-FINDINGS: Non-obvious findings of the session: API quirks, config gotchas, vendor-specific surprises.
facts.BODY-REPOSITORY-MAP: A repository map: top-level layout and what each directory or component holds.
facts.BODY-DECISIONS-IN-FORCE: The architectural and policy decisions still in force, in long form.
facts.BODY-RECENT-COMMIT-CHAIN: The recent commit chain (last ~25, oneline format), so the cold reader sees velocity and direction.
facts.BODY-PRECEDENCE-POINTER: A pointer noting that the WAL is the canonical living state and supersedes this snapshot if they diverge.

p.what-the-item-groups-answer: Items 1–4 answer "what do I do right now"; items 5–9 answer "what must I know before I trust myself here"; item 10 keeps the file honest about its own rank.

facts.WRITE-AT-EVERY-EXPLICIT-WIND-DOWN: **At every explicit wind-down** (the command below). Mandatory.
facts.WRITE-BEFORE-A-MACHINE-SWITCH: **Before a machine switch** — the other machine gets the tour.
facts.WRITE-BEFORE-A-LONG-GAP: **Before a long gap** — a vacation, weeks on another project; future you is a cold reader too.

p.any-session-end-is-a-fine-time: Any session end is a fine time; the wind-down makes it non-optional.

p.WIND-DOWN-IS-THE-EXPLICIT-FORM-OF-THE-HO: The wind-down is the explicit form of the session-end hook.

p.SHIP-TRIGGER-PHRASES: Ship trigger phrases: `END SESSION`, `WRAP UP`, `CHECKPOINT AND CLOSE`.

p.RECOGNISE-THE-INTENT-NOT-THE-EXACT-WORDI: Recognise the intent, not the exact wording.

p.A-PROJECT-MAY-ADD-NATIVE-LANGUAGE-TWINS: A project may add native-language twins in its agent instructions — the origin project of this flow runs a bilingual Russian/English set.

facts.STEP-REWRITE-THE-WAL: **Rewrite `vibevm/vibespecs/WAL.xml`** per [`session-end-hook.xml`](session-end-hook.xml): fresh date line, current phase, constraints, next step.
facts.STEP-COMMIT-IN-TOPIC-GROUPED-COMMITS: **Commit in topic-grouped commits.** The snapshot and the WAL update are checkpoint commits; a code or config change landed by the same session is a separate commit.
facts.STEP-PUSH-ONLY-IF-AUTONOMY-SANCTIONS-IT: **Push only if the project's autonomy rules sanction it.** No standing autonomy — stop at drafts or at local commits, per the hook's propose-by-default rule.
facts.STEP-EMIT-A-CHAT-TLDR: **Emit a chat TL;DR** of what the wind-down did: files written, commits created, push status, what the next session should pick up first. One screen; enough detail to verify without opening files.

p.the-point-of-the-command: The point of the command is to make session-boundary loss-of-context cheap: any session can end at any time and be resumed from `CONTINUE.md` plus the WAL with no degradation.

p.TREAT-IT-AS-A-HARD-CONTRACT-NOT-A-COURTE: Treat it as a hard contract, not a courtesy.

p.RESUME-TRIGGER-PHRASES: Trigger phrases: `RESUME SESSION`, `RESTORE CONTEXT` (and twins — recognise the intent).

p.THE-JOB-IS-TO-RESTORE-CONTEXT-AND-REPORT: The job is to **restore context and report — nothing else**:

facts.RESUME-STEP-RUN-THE-BOOT-SEQUENCE: Run the project's boot sequence (whatever its agent instructions define), then read `CONTINUE.md` and `vibevm/vibespecs/WAL.xml`.
facts.RESUME-STEP-VERIFY-THE-REPOSITORY-EMPIRI: Verify the repository state empirically: current branch, sync with the remote, working-tree status, recent commits. Never take the snapshot's word for what the tree looks like.
facts.RESUME-STEP-EMIT-A-STATUS-REPORT: Emit a status report: where work stands, active blockers, and the candidate next steps.
facts.RESUME-STEP-STOP-AND-WAIT-FOR-DIRECTION: **Stop and wait for direction.** No code edits, no commits, no pushes.

p.A-RECORDED-POINTER-IS-A-CANDIDATE-NOT-AU: Any "resume work at …" pointer in `CONTINUE.md` or the WAL names the *candidate* next step for the report — it is not authorisation to start it.

p.why-the-resume-boundary-exists: The resume boundary exists so the owner can inspect the restored state and steer, possibly somewhere other than the recorded next step.

p.booting-into-execution-takes-the-decisio: A session that boots straight into execution takes that decision away from the owner.

p.the-misfire-that-produced-the-rule: This rule is written down because exactly that misfire happened once: a resumed session read the recorded pointer as a work order and began executing, when the owner wanted a report.

p.boundary-explicit-ever-since: The boundary has been explicit ever since.

p.WAL-IS-CANONICAL-CONTINUE-IS-A-SNAPSHOT: `vibevm/vibespecs/WAL.xml` is canonical; `CONTINUE.md` is a snapshot of the moment the last wind-down ran.

p.ON-DISAGREEMENT-TRUST-THE-WAL-AND-FLAG-I: When they disagree — and they will, whenever a session updates the WAL without a full wind-down — trust the WAL and flag the divergence in your report.

p.THE-SAME-RULE-COVERS-ANY-OTHER-SNAPSHOT: The same rule covers any other snapshot: a plan document's status line, a README's "current state" paragraph.

p.THE-LIVING-CHECKPOINT-BEATS-A-FROZEN-SNA: The living checkpoint beats a frozen snapshot, always.

facts.NEVER-APPEND-TO-CONTINUE: Never append to `CONTINUE.md` — overwrite it wholesale.
facts.NEVER-WRITE-THE-SNAPSHOT-FROM-MEMORY-ALO: Never write the snapshot from memory alone — verify branch, tree, and commits empirically first.
facts.NEVER-START-EXECUTING-AFTER-A-RESUME-COM: Never start executing after a resume command — report, then wait.
facts.NEVER-TREAT-CONTINUE-AS-OVERRIDING-THE-W: Never treat `CONTINUE.md` as overriding the WAL.
facts.NEVER-SKIP-THE-CHAT-TLDR-ON-A-WIND-DOWN: Never skip the chat TL;DR on a wind-down: it is how the user verifies the checkpoint without opening files.

facts.SUM-CONTINUE-IS-THE-COLD-READERS-TOUR: `CONTINUE.md` at the repo root is the cold reader's tour: TL;DR, state, blocker, recipe, findings, map, decisions, commits, quick-start — overwritten wholesale, never appended.
facts.SUM-WHEN-TO-WRITE-IT: Write it at every wind-down, before machine switches, before gaps.
facts.SUM-WIND-DOWN-SHAPE: Wind-down: snapshot + WAL rewrite + topic-grouped commits + sanctioned push + chat TL;DR.
facts.SUM-RESUME-SHAPE: Resume: boot, read both files, verify empirically, report, stop.
facts.SUM-A-RECORDED-NEXT-STEP-IS-A-CANDIDATE: A recorded next step is a candidate, not authorisation.
facts.SUM-THE-WAL-SUPERSEDES-THE-SNAPSHOT: The WAL supersedes the snapshot wherever they diverge.
